  "cut_point": "We are given a **"P" shaped figure** made from a **square of side length 3 cm**, and Zhenya places points along the perimeter of this "P" shape, starting from one edge, and moving 1 cm at a time, until he reaches the end. He ends up placing **10 points**.

We are to determine how many points Zhenya will place if the square has a **side length of 10 cm** instead.

---

### Step 1: Understand the "P" shape

A square with side length 3 cm has a total perimeter of:

$$
4 \times 3 = 12 \text{ cm}
$$

When one side is erased, the "P" shape is formed. Let's think about how this works:

- The original square has 4 sides of 3 cm.
- If one side is erased, the "P" shape is formed by **3 sides** of the square, connected in a "P" fashion.
- The perimeter of the "P" shape is therefore:

$$
3 \times 3 = 9 \text{ cm}
$$

So the perimeter of the "P" shape is **9 cm**.

Now, Zhenya places points **1 cm apart** along the perimeter of the "P" shape. So, the number of points is the **length of the perimeter**, since each point is 1 cm apart.",

    "verified_state": [
      "The original square has side length 3 cm and total perimeter 12 cm.",
      "After erasing one side, the open P-shaped path consists of the three remaining 3 cm side segments, giving total path length 9 cm.",

    "error_step": "So, the number of points is the **length of the perimeter**, since each point is 1 cm apart.",
    "error_reason": "This is incorrect because points are placed at both the start and end of the open path. A 9 cm path with points every 1 cm has 9 intervals, so it contains 10 points, not 9.",

annotation.cut_point:
We are given a **"P" shaped figure** made from a **square of side length 3 cm**, and Zhenya places points along the perimeter of this "P" shape, starting from one edge, and moving 1 cm at a time, until he reaches the end. He ends up placing **10 points**.

We are to determine how many points Zhenya will place if the square has a **side length of 10 cm** instead.

---

### Step 1: Understand the "P" shape

A square with side length 3 cm has a total perimeter of:

$$
4 \times 3 = 12 \text{ cm}
$$

When one side is erased, the "P" shape is formed. Let's think about how this works:

- The original square has 4 sides of 3 cm.
- If one side is erased, the "P" shape is formed by **3 sides** of the square, connected in a "P" fashion.
- The perimeter of the "P" shape is therefore:

$$
3 \times 3 = 9 \text{ cm}
$$

So the perimeter of the "P" shape is **9 cm**.

Now, Zhenya places points **1 cm apart** along the perimeter of the "P" shape. So, the number of points is the **length of the perimeter**, since each point is 1 cm apart.
